title: Seven Days Later: Re-Measuring the Biggest Affirmation App — and Ourselves
description: Seven days after our I am teardown, we re-measured the winner with the same definitions: 739,613 US ratings (+827 in 7 days), still #1 on all three search terms, prices and screenshots identical, Instagram +3,436 followers — and graded our own five commitments, including 7 posts a day that earned 5 likes because the format was not copied.
markdown:
# Seven Days Later: Re-Measuring the Biggest Affirmation App — and Ourselves

*We run Anicca, a small daily affirmation app. On November 12 we published a full teardown of "I am," the biggest affirmation app on the store, and promised to re-measure everything in 7 days and publish the follow-up, whatever the numbers said. This is that follow-up. All numbers were measured on November 19, 2026, from primary sources (the App Store listing, Apple's lookup and search APIs, the app's review feed, and its Instagram account) unless a source is explicitly marked as a third-party estimate. The first teardown is here: https://aniccaai.com/blog/i-am-affirmation-app-deep-dive-en*

---

## The winner, seven days later

**I am – Daily Affirmations** by Monkey Taps, on the store since May 13, 2014. In seven days, almost nothing about its machine changed — and that is the finding.

- **739,613 US ratings at 4.83 stars** — up **827 ratings in 7 days (about 118 a day)**, right in line with the ~100+/day pace we estimated last week. Japan: 1,779 ratings, up exactly **1** in the same week. The engine is the US store.
- **Still #1 in US search** for "daily affirmations", "affirmation", and "positive affirmations" — all three, re-measured today. The #2 spot in each is still its sister app, Motivation – Daily quotes (1,080,540 ratings). The studio still owns the shelf.
- **Two new versions in seven days**: 7.9.0 on November 12 and **7.10.0 on November 18** — a release roughly every six days. The 7.10.0 release notes add new themes and affirmations, and end with the same line as every release before it: *"Love the app? Tell us in the reviews section! We read all of them."* The review engine is not a campaign. It is a habit printed at the bottom of every release.
- **Price ladder: byte-for-byte identical.** All ten in-app purchases re-read today: monthly $9.99 / $14.99, yearly $11.99 / $47.99 / $59.99 / $69.99, Lifetime **$89.99**. The quiet $11.99 "a year priced like a month" offer is still there.
- **Store screenshots: identical.** All nine US screenshot URLs match last week's set exactly. Subtitle unchanged: "Positive widgets & motivation." Fourteen languages, unchanged.

Here is the storefront we re-read today — the same nine screenshots, selling the same one thing: a widget.

## Instagram: the machine, one week on

@iam.affirmations grew from 1,819,003 to **1,822,439 followers (+3,436 in 7 days)** and from 5,557 to **5,594 posts (+37 net, about 5.3 a day)**. We pulled all 37 posts from the last seven days:

- **Format mix: 48.6% video, 35.1% image, 16.2% carousel** — statistically the same recipe as last week (47 / 33 / 20).
- Average likes this week ran **image 1,674 > carousel 1,029 > video 873** — a different order than the week we first measured. But the two biggest posts were both videos, and both were *date-claims*:
  - **November 14, video, 4,730 likes, 56 comments**: a "2027 is my year of clarity and wealth" declaration that ends with *"Type YES to claim it."* [See it here](https://www.instagram.com/reel/Dful3XaF1FA/)
  - **November 16, video, 2,555 likes, 791 comments**: the post is simply titled "November 16." — *"This week, something you've been waiting for finally arrives… Type YES to claim it."* 791 comments is more than 200× the week's median post (~3 comments). [See it here](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfzhfmVBcqf/)
  - The week's top image (3,212 likes) was, again, an ad for the product itself: *"I turned my lock screen into a pep talk I actually believe."* [See it here](https://www.instagram.com/p/DfuRGnKkfph/)

The CTA grammar did not change at all: **Type YES** (comment a keyword), **save this** (bookmark), **screenshot this and put it somewhere you'll see it** (move the post onto the reader's own phone), **send this to someone**. Direct app promotion appeared once in 37 posts. The other 36 were participation and saving.

Reviews told the same story as last week. Of the 50 most recent US reviews, 38 are five stars: morning habit, mindset, notifications that remind people to say the words out loud, years of use. The one-star complaints this week were about the app "not being free" after onboarding questions lead into a trial, and about notifications a user could not stop — the winner still bleeds on billing clarity and control, not on the product.

## What we learned

1. **Nothing changing is the strategy.** In seven days the winner changed its content and nothing else — not prices, not screenshots, not the subtitle, not the format mix, not the release-note footer. Consistency at volume is not a phase of their growth. It is the growth.
2. **The release cadence is part of the review engine.** A version roughly every six days, each one ending with the same review request, compounds into ~118 new ratings a day. The ask is small, identical, and forever.
3. **Date-claims are the comment engine.** A post that names *today's date* and asks readers to claim what is arriving outperformed everything else on comments by two orders of magnitude. The mechanic is the date, not production value — these are 8-second text videos.
4. **Volume is copyable in a week. Format and mechanics are not.** We proved this on ourselves, below.

## The scorecard: what we promised on November 12

Last week's article ended with five commitments. Here is each one, graded with measured numbers:

| Commitment | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Fix the lifetime anchor | **Done on the store — with a stale copy bug left behind** | Our US listing's in-app purchases now show **Lifetime $89.99** (was $59.99, the same as yearly). But our description text still prints "Lifetime — $59.99". The store's price list is the source of truth; the copy is stale and we are disclosing it instead of quietly leaving it |
| Copy the comment mechanic + date-event calendar | **Not done** | None of our sampled captions this week carried a Type-YES-style CTA |
| Treat the widget as a measured channel | **Not measured** | We still do not count widget glances. Writing "not measured" again is the honest entry |
| Add the review line to release notes | **Not done** | Our 1.10.0 release notes have no review request, and our in-app rating prompt was shown **0 times** in the Nov 11–17 window |
| Re-measure in 7 days and publish | **Done** | This article |

And the rest of our week, measured: **Anicca 1.10.0 shipped on November 18** with personalized onboarding and a soft paywall. In the Nov 11–17 window we had 605 store impressions → 154 page views → **3 downloads** (all in Japan; the US funnel was 200 → 9 → 0), 18 paywall views, 6 purchase starts, **0 completed purchases**. Five active paid subscriptions, unchanged. Our MRR was last confirmed at $20 on November 7 and has not been re-measured since — we will not print a fresher number we do not have.

On Instagram, the split is the whole lesson. Our English account did copy the winner's *volume*: exactly **7 posts a day** from November 14 to 18. But of the 47 posts we could pull, **all 47 were images — 0% video, 0% carousel** — against the winner's 48.6% video. Total result for the week: **5 likes, 0 comments, followers unchanged at 3.** The winner's 37 posts earned thousands of likes and a 791-comment thread in the same seven days.

## The gap, updated

| Metric | I am | Anicca (us) |
|---|---|---|
| US ratings | 739,613 (+827 this week) | **1** (+0) |
| US search rank, "daily affirmations" | #1 | Outside the top 8 on every tracked keyword (day 8 of baseline) |
| Instagram followers | 1,822,439 (+3,436 this week) | **3** (+0) |
| Posts per day (Instagram) | ~5.3 net (37 in 7 days) | 7.0 — volume copied |
| Video share of posts | 48.6% | **0%** in the 47 posts pulled |
| Engagement this week | Top post 4,730 likes; top thread 791 comments | 5 likes, 0 comments, total |
| Lifetime price | $89.99 | **$89.99** (fixed; description copy still stale) |
| 7-day downloads | Not public | 3 (US: 0) |
| Purchases | Not public | 0 completed (6 started) |

## What we do next, in order

1. **Fix the format, not the volume.** Production switches to the winner's mix — video first (≈47–49%), then image, then carousel — on the same 7-a-day cadence. Volume without the mix earned us 5 likes; we will not run another week of it.
2. **Put the mechanic in the creative.** Date-claim and Type-YES CTAs, save-this carousels, screenshot-this posts — copied from the winner's actual posts above, tied to the calendar.
3. **Add the review line to our release notes** and show the system rating prompt after a value moment — the two cheapest items on last week's list, still undone. They go into the next release, not a backlog.
4. **Correct the stale lifetime price in our store description** so the copy matches the $89.99 the store actually charges.
5. **Re-measure again in 7 days** (November 26) with the same definitions, and publish the third report. The next full teardown in this series takes on the #2 app on the same shelf — Motivation – Daily quotes, 1,080,540 ratings, same studio, same template.

## Copy this to your agent

If you published a teardown with commitments, paste this into your agent (Muse, Grok, Codex — any of them) and run the follow-up exactly like this:

```text
You are my follow-up researcher. Exactly 7 days ago we published a teardown
of our category winner with dated commitments. Re-measure, using only free
sources, with the SAME definitions as the first pass:

1. Pull the winner's listing again (lookup API + store page): version and
   release date, rating count and score, every in-app purchase price,
   screenshot URLs. Diff each field against the first measurement and
   report the delta, including "identical" where nothing changed.
2. Re-check search rank for the same keywords, same storefront.
3. Pull the winner's social profile and every post since the first
   measurement. Report net posts/day, format mix, average engagement per
   format, and the top 3 posts with URLs and their exact CTA mechanics.
4. Read the 50 most recent reviews. Report the star distribution and
   whether last time's praise/complaint themes persisted.
5. Grade EVERY commitment from the first article as done / partial /
   not done / not measured, each with a measured number. Where our own
   number does not exist, write "not measured" — never estimate our side.
6. Write it as: winner delta → what we learned → the commitment
   scorecard → updated winner-vs-us table → next actions in order.
   Mark third-party estimates as estimates and anything unobtained
   as "not obtained".
7. Save the research file, publish the article, hand the same text to
   every channel, and schedule the next re-measurement in 7 days.
```

We ran the first teardown with the prompt in last week's article, and this follow-up with the one above. The full research file behind this article — every measurement, source URL, and screenshot link — is kept with our team's working files, and this series continues weekly.

## Our wins and losses, on the record

**Losses:** Seven posts a day for a week produced 5 likes, 0 comments, and 0 new followers, because the format and the mechanics were not copied — only the count was. Our US store funnel converted 200 impressions into 0 downloads. Six purchase starts produced zero completed purchases. Two of the five things we promised in print — the release-note review line and the widget metric — were simply not done, and a third (the comment mechanic) exists only in our article, not in our posts. Our store description still shows a lifetime price the store no longer charges.

**Wins:** The lifetime anchor is actually fixed at the store level — $89.99, the winner's exact price. Version 1.10.0 shipped with the personalized onboarding and soft paywall the first teardown called for. Downloads tripled week over week (1 → 3) and page views rose 14 → 154 — small numbers, printed as-is. The volume discipline held for a full week. And the follow-up itself exists, on the promised date, with the scorecard graded against us. That is the compounding this series is for: make something people want, measure the winner, publish the losses, and re-measure in 7 days.

*Sources: App Store listings for I am – Daily Affirmations and Anicca (read Nov 19, 2026); Apple iTunes Lookup and Search APIs (Nov 19, 2026); I am US review feed, most recent 50 (Nov 19, 2026); Instagram @iam.affirmations and @anicca.en profiles and posts via connector (Nov 19, 2026); our own App Store Connect aggregates (window Nov 11–17, 2026) and Mixpanel window (Nov 11–17, 2026); first measurement: our teardown of November 12, 2026. Revenue for I am (~$702K/month) remains an October 2026 third-party estimate (Airbridge) and was not re-measured this week.*
